flagged.title: Signed Binary, Addition, Subtraction and Shifts
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly states that 00000010 is positive 5 and 10000010 is negative 5 (00000010 is 2, whereas 5 is 00000101), teaching an incorrect binary conversion that would cost marks in a GCSE exam.

mark_affecting.video_says: if 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0 is positive 5, you just flip that very first bit on the left to a 1, giving you 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, and boom, suddenly you have negative 5.

flagged.title: Graphics: Pixels, Resolution and Colour Depth
flagged.reason: The video explicitly teaches an incorrect unit rule that 1 KB = 1000 bytes and claims writing KB instead of KiB will cost marks, which can lead students to wrongly define a kilobyte as 1,000 bytes or use incorrect units in Eduqas/WJEC exams where a kilobyte is defined as 1,024 bytes.

mark_affecting.quote: 1 KiB equals 1,024 bytes... 1 KB equals 1,000 bytes. If you write KB instead of KiB, or if you divide by 1,000 instead of 1,024 in a calculation question, it will definitely cost you a mark.

flagged.title: Storage Units, Capacity and Compression
flagged.reason: The video teaches non-specification IEC unit names (kibibyte/KiB, mebibyte/MiB, gibibyte/GiB) instead of the exam specification's required base-2 units (kilobyte/KB, megabyte/MB, gigabyte/GB), which would confuse students and lose marks.

mark_affecting.quote: 1024 bytes gives us a kibibyte, or KiB... mebibyte or MiB... gibibyte... Notice that little 'i' in the abbreviation? That stands for binary and proves we're working in base-2.
